statement: For a full final subcategory $J^\prime\subset J$ and $i_0=i\in I$, there are $j_0\in J^\prime$ and $u_0:\varphi(i_0)\to j_0$.
notes: Opening paragraph precedes the first manuscript marker in this extract; initial choice uses finality only.

statement: The recursive data comprise functors $\beta\mapsto i_\beta$ and $\beta\mapsto j_\beta$, natural arrows $u_\beta:\varphi i_\beta\to j_\beta$, and arrows $v_\beta:j_\beta\to\varphi i_{\beta+1}$ satisfying $v_\beta u_\beta=\varphi\tau_{\beta+1,\beta}$, $u_{\beta+1}v_\beta=\tau^\prime_{\beta+1,\beta}$, $\tau^\prime_{\beta^\prime,\beta}u_\beta=u_{\beta^\prime}\varphi\tau_{\beta^\prime,\beta}$ and $\varphi\tau_{\beta^\prime+1,\beta+1}v_\beta=v_{\beta^\prime}\tau^\prime_{\beta^\prime,\beta}$.
notes: Four compatibility conditions are grouped as the definition of one recursive datum; bounds on all indices retained.

statement: At stage $\alpha$, extend each previous chain by a cocone with vertices $i_\alpha,j_\alpha$, choose $u_\alpha$, and, only when $\alpha=\delta+1$, choose $v_\delta$; impose naturality of $u$ and the two adjacent-composite equations, and in the successor case naturality of $v$.
gap_or_error: Printed target $j_\beta$ in $(3_\alpha)(\beta)$ should be $j_\alpha$; printed bounds and indices include slips.
repair: Interpret the displayed equations with correctly typed targets; edition wording retained and separately registered.

statement: For $\alpha=\delta+1$, to verify naturality of $u$ at the new target, it is enough to verify the square at $\beta=\delta$.
notes: Footnote 140; earlier squares paste with this last one.

statement: At a successor $\alpha=\delta+1$, the arrows from all earlier $i_\beta$ to $i_\alpha$ and from all earlier $j_\beta$ to $j_\alpha$ are determined by the arrows from index $\delta$ and composition.
notes: The four chosen arrows are reduced to two adjacent composites.

statement: If $I$ is filtered and $\varphi:I\to J$ is final, every arrow $w:\varphi(a)\to\varphi(b)$ admits an eventual lift: there are $r:b\to c$ and $t:a\to c$ in $I$ with $\varphi(r)w=\varphi(t)$.
repair: Complete proof from a finite comma-category zigzag and a cocone is given in the block at p322.

statement: For the prescribed $u_\delta:\varphi(i_\delta)\to j_\delta$, finality of $\varphi$ and eventual lifting produce $i_{\delta+1}$, $v_\delta$ and $\tau_{\delta+1,\delta}$ with $v_\delta u_\delta=\varphi(\tau_{\delta+1,\delta})$.

After that choice, finality of $J^\prime$ supplies $u_{\delta+1}:\varphi(i_{\delta+1})\to j_{\delta+1}$; fullness supplies the unique transition $\tau^\prime_{\delta+1,\delta}=u_{\delta+1}v_\delta$ in $J^\prime$.
Do the remaining new naturality conditions $(3_\alpha)(\beta)$ and $(4_\alpha)(\beta)$ follow automatically from the two adjacent-composite equations and earlier compatibilities?
repair: Yes. The two complete composition calculations in the development block at p327 establish this directly.
notes: The source asks the question, then uses unnecessary corrective steps rather than these identities.

statement: One may enforce the new $u$-naturality squares by equalizing the final parallel pair and postcomposing $u_\alpha$ and $\tau^\prime_{\alpha,\delta}$.
gap_or_error: The printed source of the pair and two subsequent arrow indices are mistyped. The pair already agrees under the preceding construction.
repair: Correct the types in interpretation. No equalization is needed; its inclusion does not invalidate the proof.
notes: Not counted as an additional mathematical counterexample.

statement: A family of at most $|\alpha|$ parallel pairs with common target $\varphi(i_\alpha)$ can be simultaneously equalized in $J$ under the stated filteredness; finality and eventual lifting allow the equalizing map to be replaced by $\varphi(\sigma)$ for $\sigma:i_\alpha\to i^\prime$ in $I$.
notes: This supplies a valid, though unnecessary at successor stages, correction of the $v$-naturality squares.

statement: Performing any required correction of $i_\alpha,v_\delta,\tau_{\alpha,\delta}$ before the choice of $j_\alpha,u_\alpha,\tau^\prime_{\alpha,\delta}$ preserves the already imposed equations and completes the successor step.
notes: Source explicitly repairs the order of its preliminary choices.

statement: At a limit $\alpha$, filteredness for diagrams of size $|\alpha|$ supplies a cocone on $(i_\beta)_{\beta<\alpha}$ in $I$ and one on $(j_\beta)_{\beta<\alpha}$ in $J^\prime$.
gap_or_error: The displayed transition subscripts in the prose are reversed.
repair: Read $\tau_{\alpha,\beta}$ and $\tau^\prime_{\alpha,\beta}$; source retained.

statement: Finality of $J^\prime$ and filteredness allow $j_\alpha$ to be enlarged so that a map $\varphi(i_\alpha)\to j_\alpha$ exists; a simultaneous equalization in $J$, followed by passage to $J^\prime$, makes it compatible with all previous $u_\beta$.
gap_or_error: Some sources of the parallel pairs are outside $J^\prime$.
repair: Equalize in $J$, which has the required filteredness by finality from $I$, then move the vertex to $J^\prime$. This is the ambient-category reading of the source argument.

statement: Lemma 4.13.17. Let $\varphi:I\to J$ be final with $I$ filtered, and let $J^\prime\subset J$ be a full replete final subcategory. Suppose a nonzero limit ordinal $\theta$ satisfies: $I,J^\prime$ admit $\theta$-chain colimits preserved by $\varphi,J^\prime\hookrightarrow J$, and for every $\alpha<\theta$, $I$ admits cocones on diagrams of size at most $|\alpha|$. Then $I^\prime=\varphi^{-1}(J^\prime)$ is final in $I$.
repair: The block at p330 gives the final-colimit comparison and all transfinite steps explicitly.
notes: The extract begins in the proof, which started at ms313; the statement itself is wholly supplied.

statement: Under Lemma 4.13.17, $I^\prime$ is filtered, has the same indicated bounded cocones as $I$, and $I^\prime\to J^\prime$ is final.
repair: Fullness transfers cocones after moving their vertex; the comma categories for the composite into $J$ and for the functor into $J^\prime$ coincide.

statement: The proof of 4.13.17 needs only a limit ordinal, not specifically the initial ordinal of the cardinal $\pi$.
gap_or_error: Final sentence prints cardinal limite rather than ordinal limite.
repair: Read ordinal; the argument works for any nonzero limit ordinal satisfying the listed hypotheses.

statement: For a useful $\pi$ and a full replete $\underline S\subset\mathcal M$, if membership in $\underline S$ is equivalent to finality of $\underline S(\pi)/x\subset\mathcal M_\pi/x$, then $\underline S$ is exactly the essential image of $\operatorname{Ind}_{\pi^+}(\underline S(\pi))\to\mathcal M$.
gap_or_error: The first formula on p332 omits $(\pi)$ from $\underline S(\pi)/x$.
repair: Use the canonical $\pi^+$-filtered presentation and factorization of maps from presentable objects.
notes: This is the implication b to a-prime of 4.13.15; the mistaken b-to-d reference on p331 is a source slip.

statement: If $x=\varinjlim_{i\in I}x_i$ is an adapted presentation with $I$ $\pi^+$-filtered and $x_i\in\mathcal M_\pi$, and the membership criterion holds for this presentation, then $x\in\underline S$ makes $I_{\underline S}$ final; restriction to it presents x by objects of $\underline S(\pi)$ and places x in the indicated Ind-image.
notes: The forward implication needs only the filteredness and finality conditions, not that $I$ is ordered.

statement: For the reverse implication from the Ind-image to membership in an adapted presentation, the two final presentations give a pullback square over $\mathcal M_\pi/x$, and 4.13.17 transfers finality to the inverse-image index category.
gap_or_error: The choice of the initial ordinal of a possibly singular $\pi$ is justified by an incorrect stronger cofinality assertion.
repair: Use the initial ordinal $\theta=(\pi^\prime_0)^+\leq\pi$ instead; the $\mathrm L(\pi^\prime_0,\pi)$ and adaptedness hypotheses supply its colimits. This repairs the application without enlarging $\pi$.

statement: The initial ordinal of cardinality $\pi$ is large before every cardinal $\pi^\prime<\pi$.
gap_or_error: For singular $\pi$, its cofinal subset of size $\operatorname{cf}(\pi)<\pi$ is unbounded.
repair: Only an ordinal large before $\pi^\prime_0$ is needed; take $(\pi^\prime_0)^+\leq\pi$. Alternatively impose $\operatorname{cf}(\pi)>\pi^\prime_0$ if retaining the original ordinal.
notes: This false auxiliary sentence is separated from the repairable main theorem.

statement: In 4.13.15, accessibility from the small part together with closure of that part under the specified bounded colimits implies closure of the whole subcategory under the corresponding colimits.
gap_or_error: The source calls a-prime to a sorital and omits the argument.
repair: 4.13.19–21 supply the extension argument; full simultaneous-presentation calculation is given at p341.

statement: Corollary 4.13.18. Let $\pi$ be useful for $\mathcal M$ and let $\theta$ be a nonzero limit ordinal of size at most $\pi$ whose colimits exist in $\mathcal M$. For full replete $\underline S$, the following are equivalent: relative $\pi$-accessibility and closure under $\theta$-colimits; relative $\pi$-accessibility and $\theta$-closure of $\underline S(\pi)$; $\theta$-closure of $\underline S(\pi)$ and the canonical-slice finality membership criterion; that same closure and the membership criterion in every $\theta$-$\pi$-adapted presentation.
repair: Proof follows the verified 4.13.17 argument and 4.13.19. The word relative in a-prime makes explicit the ambient meaning.
notes: All hypotheses and the equivalence a,a-prime,b,c are recorded here; ordered variant separately below.

statement: A $\theta$-$\pi$-adapted presentation is a diagram of objects of $\mathcal M_\pi$ indexed by an essentially small $\pi^+$-filtered category that admits $\theta$-chain colimits, with the diagram preserving those colimits.

In Corollary 4.13.18, the condition restricted to ordered adapted presentations is equivalent to the other conditions when $\theta$ is large before a useful $\pi_0$ and $\pi^{\pi_0}=\pi$; without these extra assumptions the other conditions still imply the ordered condition.
gap_or_error: Footnote 143 prints c where its contrast and conclusion require c-prime.
repair: Restore the prime in interpretation; the extra assumptions guarantee the required ordered presentations.

statement: Lemma 4.13.19. Let $\mathcal M\simeq\operatorname{Ind}_{\pi^+}(\mathcal M_\pi)$ and let $\underline S$ be the full Ind-image of $\underline S(\pi)=\underline S\cap\mathcal M_\pi$. Assume these two small parts admit, and their inclusion preserves, colimits of one nonzero limit-ordinal shape of size at most $\pi$. If both small parts admit the shapes in a set $\Phi$, each of size at most $\pi$, and their inclusion preserves them, then $\mathcal M,\underline S$ admit $\Phi$-colimits and their inclusion preserves them.
gap_or_error: Opening hypothesis has a dropped designation of S and the ordinal-closure phrase is repeated.
repair: Use the intended two small categories and simultaneous diagram presentations from 4.11.1; complete calculation at p341.

statement: Lemma 4.13.20. For a functor $f_0:C\to C^\prime$ between essentially small categories, under the bounded-shape and limit-ordinal hypotheses of 4.11.1, if the required colimits exist and $f_0$ preserves them, then $\operatorname{Ind}_{\pi^+}(f_0)$ preserves the same colimits.
repair: Represent the entire source diagram over a common filtered index and interchange the two colimits; detailed proof at p341.

statement: The extension assertion should hold for $f_0:C\to\mathcal N$ where $\mathcal N$ admits $\pi^+$-filtered colimits, using the canonical filtered-colimit extension instead of requiring $\mathcal N$ itself to be an Ind-completion.
gap_or_error: Footnote 144 contains an editorial [?] and fragmentary wording, including the notation Ind_pi(C,N).
repair: The same displayed proof works when C has the stated bounded colimits and f0 preserves them; no conjectural reconstruction of the illegible word is inserted into the source.

statement: Corollary 4.13.21, first case. Under 4.13.20, if $\Phi$ contains all shapes of size at most $\pi$, then $\operatorname{Ind}_{\pi^+}(f_0)$ preserves all small colimits.
repair: A small category is the $\pi^+$-filtered union of its subcategories generated by at most $\pi$ arrows; use iterated colimits.

statement: Corollary 4.13.21, second case. Under 4.13.20, if $\Phi$ contains all filtered shapes of size at most $\pi$, the extension preserves all small filtered colimits.
repair: Enlarge bounded subcategories to bounded filtered subcategories and use the resulting filtered union; compare 4.13.38–39.

statement: Corollary 4.13.21, third case. Under 4.13.20 and its ordinal hypothesis, if $\Phi$ contains all shapes large before $\pi_0$ of size at most $\pi$, the extension preserves all small colimits indexed by categories large before $\pi_0$.
gap_or_error: The usual bounded-index decomposition needs a cardinal sharpness bound not stated explicitly in this variant; the single ordinal-chain hypothesis has not been shown here to remove that need.
repair: A complete proof is supplied under the sufficient additional condition pi^{pi0}=pi in the envelope development at p355. The unrestricted fixed-rank implication is not independently certified and is not labelled false.
notes: Do not identify this with preservation of arbitrary colimits.

statement: Corollary 4.13.21, fourth case. Under 4.13.20, if $\Phi$ contains all discrete categories of size at most $\pi$, the extension preserves all small coproducts.
repair: Index a family by the $\pi^+$-filtered poset of its subsets of size at most $\pi$, and take the iterated coproduct.

statement: The respective converses in 4.13.21 follow by restricting preservation to the indicated small diagrams in C.
repair: The canonical inclusions preserve those small colimits under the standing hypotheses, so restriction recovers the f0 comparisons.

statement: Theorem 4.13.22. Suppose $\pi$ is useful for accessible $\mathcal M$, $\Phi$ is a set of essentially small shapes with reduced size at most $\pi$ containing a nonzero limit ordinal, and $\mathcal M$ admits $\Phi$-colimits. For full replete $\underline S$, the following are equivalent: relative $\pi$-accessibility and ambient $\Phi$-closure; relative $\pi$-accessibility and $\Phi$-closure of $\underline S(\pi)$; that small-part closure plus membership detected by finality of $\underline S(\pi)/x$ in $\mathcal M_\pi/x$; that closure plus membership detected by finality of $I_{\underline S}$ in every $\Phi$-$\pi$-adapted presentation of x.
repair: Combine 4.13.17 with 4.13.19 and the canonical presentation. The proof and its distinct roles are explained in blocks p330,p338,p341.
notes: The theorem is a synthesis of the preceding proofs, rather than a new proof written out in full here.

statement: A $\Phi$-$\pi$-adapted presentation is a diagram of $\pi^+$-presentable objects over an essentially small $\pi^+$-filtered category admitting $\Phi$-colimits, with the diagram preserving them.

In 4.13.22, if $\pi^{\pi_0}=\pi$ for a useful $\pi_0\leq\pi$ and every shape in $\Phi$ is large before $\pi_0$, the criterion restricted to ordered adapted presentations is equivalent to a,a-prime,b,c. Without those additional hypotheses it is still implied by them.
notes: Footnotes 146–147 expressly distinguish the unconditional implication and defer a better formulation to pp359–360.

statement: Definition 4.13.23. A full subcategory $\underline S\subset\mathcal M$ is $\Phi$-$\pi$-accessible in $\mathcal M$ when $\pi$ is useful for $\mathcal M$, $\mathcal M$ admits $\Phi$-colimits, $\underline S$ is relatively $\pi$-accessible, and it is closed under the ambient $\Phi$-colimits.
notes: The limit-ordinal condition is unnecessary merely to introduce this definition.

statement: For $\Phi$ consisting of one ordinal shape, the abbreviation is ordinal–$\pi$-accessible; for $\Phi$ the shapes of size at most $\pi$ large before $\pi_0$, it is $\pi_0$–$\pi$-accessible.
notes: Footnote 151.

statement: Under the ambient hypotheses, Definition 4.13.23 is equivalent to the corresponding replete-subcategory conditions of Theorem 4.13.22; the difficult implication is that membership in an accessible closed subcategory forces cofinal occurrence of its objects in every adapted presentation.
notes: This statement describes the operational content of the theorem, not an unrestricted assertion about arbitrary presentations.

statement: Proposition 4.13.24 with its limit-ordinal hypothesis retained. Intersection with $\mathcal M_\pi$ and taking the full Ind-image give inverse order-preserving bijections between relatively $\pi$-accessible ambient $\Phi$-closed subcategories of $\mathcal M$ and replete $\Phi$-closed subcategories of $\mathcal M_\pi$.
repair: Ordinal colimits split idempotents in the small subcategory; presentables in its Ind-image are its retracts; apply 4.13.19. Full explanation at p345.
notes: The separate footnote weakening is false, as recorded next.

statement: In Proposition 4.13.24, the condition that $\Phi$ contain a nonzero limit ordinal can simply be omitted with no replacement.
gap_or_error: Then the stated small subcategories need not be closed under retracts, and Ind-completion changes their small parts.
repair: Require retract closure separately, or retain the ordinal hypothesis. The replete full subcategory of two-element sets with $\Phi=\varnothing$ gives an explicit counterexample: its $\aleph_1$-filtered Ind-image contains a singleton.
notes: Footnote 152; full proof marked ours in the development block at p345.

statement: Proposition 4.13.25. Under 4.13.23 and $I_{\alpha_\pi}\in\Phi$, the replete $\Phi$-$\pi$-accessible full subcategories of $\mathcal M$ are closed under intersections indexed by at most $\pi$ objects, with the manuscript footnote restricting the bound to strictly less than $\pi$ when $\pi$ is a limit cardinal.
notes: The correction in footnote 153 belongs to the source statement; do not discard it. The purely typographical cardinal Phi is editorially corrected to pi.

statement: The correspondence $\mathcal S\mapsto\mathcal S\cap\mathcal M_\pi$ and $B\mapsto\operatorname{Ind}_\pi(B)$ preserves inclusions. The intersection assertion follows with the cardinal/cofinality hypotheses of 4.13.25.
notes: An order isomorphism alone preserves lattice meets, not necessarily the literal ambient intersection without the cofinality argument.

statement: 4.13.26. For a replete full inclusion $f:\mathcal S\hookrightarrow\mathcal M$, $\Phi$-$\pi$-accessibility means: $\pi$ is useful for both categories; both admit $\Phi$-colimits; $f$ preserves them and $\pi^+$-filtered colimits; and $f(\mathcal S_\pi)\subset\mathcal M_\pi$.
notes: In modern notation, objects in M_pi are pi^+-presentable; this translates the manuscript convention involving diagrams of at most pi arrows.

statement: When the cardinal is increased from $\pi$ to $\pi'>\pi$, existence and preservation of the fixed $\Phi$-colimits and preservation of the indicated sufficiently filtered colimits remain valid.
notes: The classes of pi-prime-filtered index categories are smaller; no cardinal arithmetic is used here.

statement: If $\pi_0$ is useful for $\mathcal M,\mathcal S$ and $\pi'>\pi_0$ satisfies $(\pi')^{\pi_0}=\pi'$, then $\pi'$ is useful for both categories.
GCH makes $(\pi')^{\pi_0}=\pi'$ automatic for every infinite $\pi'>\pi_0$.
gap_or_error: This fails at singular cardinals of cofinality at most pi0.
repair: Retain the exponentiation hypothesis, or under GCH impose cf(pi-prime)>pi0. For pi0=aleph_0 and pi-prime=aleph_omega, König diagonalization gives (pi-prime)^{aleph_0}>pi-prime independently of GCH.
references: BrookeTaylorRosicky2017, Section 2 (modern rank comparison); direct cardinal proof in commentary
notes: The failure is in the cardinal-arithmetic inference. No claim is made that every final category-theoretic conclusion mentioned under GCH must consequently fail.

statement: If $f$ is $\pi_0$-accessible and $\pi'\geq\max(\pi,\operatorname{cardred}\mathcal S_{\pi_0})$ with $(\pi')^{\pi_0}=\pi'$, then $f(\mathcal S_{\pi'})\subset\mathcal M_{\pi'}$.

Proposition 4.13.27. A $\Phi$-$\pi$-accessible replete full subcategory remains $\Phi$-$\pi'$-accessible under the explicit rank hypotheses $(\pi')^{\pi_0}=\pi'$ and $\pi'\geq\operatorname{cardred}\mathcal S_{\pi_0}$, with $\pi'>\pi\geq\pi_0$ and the stated usefulness/accessibility assumptions.
gap_or_error: The printed adjective adaptee is the wrong term for a subcategory.
repair: Read accessible, as in the preceding discussion; keep the explicit exponentiation assumption.

statement: A sufficient explicit enlargement is $\pi'=2^c$, where $c$ is infinite and bounds $\pi$ and $\operatorname{cardred}\mathcal S(\pi)$.
repair: $(2^c)^{\pi_0}=2^{c\cdot\pi_0}=2^c$; Cantor gives $2^c>\pi$ when $c\geq\pi$.
notes: This construction is valid in ZFC and avoids the defective GCH shortcut.

statement: Proposition 4.13.28. If each shape in $\Phi$ is filtered, finite unions of $\Phi$-$\pi$-accessible object classes are $\Phi$-$\pi$-accessible. More generally this holds for unions indexed by a set of size at most $\lambda<\pi$ if every shape in $\Phi$ is $\lambda^+$-filtered.
repair: The omitted finite/cofinal pigeonhole argument is supplied in the p350 exposition.

statement: Corollary 4.13.29. The replete accessible and accessibly embedded object classes in an accessible category are closed under small unions.
repair: Choose one sufficiently large rank for the small family and its indexing set, then apply 4.13.28.

statement: Lemma 4.13.30. Let $I$ be $\pi^+$-filtered and $\{J_r:r\in A\}$ full subcategories with $|A|\leq\pi$. If their union is objectwise cofinal in $I$, some $J_r\hookrightarrow I$ is final.
repair: If none is objectwise cofinal choose i_r with no arrow into J_r, then a common upper bound for the i_r. An arrow from that bound into the union is a contradiction. A full objectwise cofinal subcategory of a filtered category is filtered and final. Complete proof in commentary.

statement: Theorem 4.13.31. If $f:\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$ is accessible and $\mathcal T\subset\mathcal N$ is a replete accessible, accessibly embedded full subcategory, then the full inverse image $f^{-1}\mathcal T$ is accessible and accessibly embedded in $\mathcal M$.
repair: The modern proof is the pseudopullback of f and the replete full inclusion; the source proves it by a cofinal presentation criterion. Choose sufficiently large common ranks in its quantitative proof.
references: MakkaiPare1989, Theorem 5.1.6 (cited and explained by Positselski2024Limits); BrookeTaylorRosicky2017, proof of Theorem 3.2, Step 1

statement: Corollary 4.13.32 gives a quantitative inverse-image criterion from: $\mathcal T$ is $\pi_0$-$\pi$-accessible in $\mathcal N$; $\pi_0$ useful for $\mathcal M$; $f(\mathcal M_\pi)\subset\mathcal N_\pi$; and $\mathcal M$ has $\pi_0^+$-filtered colimits preserved by $f$.
gap_or_error: The printed conclusion says in N instead of in M. The proof also uses pi useful for M, which is not literally condition b).
repair: Read M in the conclusion and include pi useful for M, for example by choosing pi>pi0 with pi^{pi0}=pi. This suffices for the theorem 4.13.31 and its intended rank choice.
notes: The unrestricted quantitative statement is not certified without the additional usefulness/rank condition; the qualitative theorem is certified.

statement: The full inverse image $\mathcal S$ is closed under the $\pi_0^+$-filtered colimits in $\mathcal M$, since $f$ preserves them and $\mathcal T$ is closed under them.
With $\mathcal S(\pi)=\mathcal S\cap\mathcal M_\pi$, the canonical functor $\operatorname{Ind}_\pi\mathcal S(\pi)\to\mathcal S$ is fully faithful.
notes: This uses compactness in M and the inherited sufficiently filtered colimits, not fullness of f.

statement: For $x\in\mathcal S$, the canonical presentation indexed by $I=\mathcal M_\pi/x$ is $\pi_0$-$\pi$-adapted when $\pi$ is useful for $\mathcal M$ and $\mathcal M$ satisfies $L_{\pi_0}$.
gap_or_error: The sentence invoking b) tacitly requires the rank repair to 4.13.32.
repair: Use the strengthened rank choice recorded above.

statement: Applying $f$ to that canonical presentation gives a $\pi_0$-$\pi$-adapted presentation of $f(x)$, because it preserves the prescribed colimits and sends $\mathcal M_\pi$ into $\mathcal N_\pi$.
notes: The circled cross-reference 1 in the text should refer to condition d).

statement: The indices with $f(x_i)\in\mathcal T$ form a cofinal full subcategory $I'\subset I$, so $x\simeq\varinjlim_{I'}x_i$ with $x_i\in\mathcal S(\pi)$; hence the above Ind functor is essentially surjective.
notes: The first use of S in the tuple (N,pi0,pi,S) is an uncorrected source slip for T; the following source editorial bracket already corrects a second occurrence.

statement: Question 4.13.33 conjectures that the replete full essential image of every accessible functor between accessible categories is accessible and accessibly embedded; equivalently the functor factors through such a full image.
gap_or_error: The source itself rejects the assertion in footnote 156.
repair: False in ZFC: the accessible forgetful functor from chosen split monomorphisms of posets to the arrow category has full image the split monomorphisms, not closed under lambda-filtered colimits for any regular lambda. A complete ordinal-chain counterexample is supplied.
notes: The source proof_status records the conjectural presentation; the counterexample and the source retraction are recorded here as present status.

statement: The same essential-image conjecture is false even after closing the image under retracts (natural-closure in the manuscript).
repair: The class of split monomorphisms in Pos^[1] is already closed under retracts. The same ordinal-chain example therefore applies.
notes: This is the explicit content of manuscript footnotes 156–157, not a new gap attributed to Grothendieck.

statement: If $\mathcal M$ is accessible with $\pi_0^+$-filtered colimits and $A$ is a small full subcategory, the smallest replete full subcategory containing $A$ and closed under those colimits is conjectured accessible and accessibly embedded.
repair: A proof at a sufficiently large rank, by bounded closure and filtered subcategory completion, is supplied in the p355 development.
notes: No claim of priority: the development extends the argument of 4.13.34; an exact matching published statement was not located in the checked sources.

statement: The same small-envelope conjecture is made after additionally closing under a small family $\Phi$ of small colimit shapes which exist in $\mathcal M$.
repair: The p355 development proves this more general version, using the same bounded closure and the Ind extension theorem 4.13.19.

statement: Proposition 4.13.34. In an accessible category with all small filtered colimits, a replete full subcategory is accessible, accessibly embedded and closed under filtered colimits iff it is the filtered-colimit closure of a small full subcategory.

For an accessibly embedded $\pi$-accessible subcategory, its $\pi$-presentable part generates it under $\pi^+$-filtered colimits; if it is closed under all filtered colimits this same part generates its filtered-colimit envelope.
For a small $A\subset\mathcal M_\pi$, its closure $B$ under filtered colimits with at most $\pi$ arrows remains in $\mathcal M_\pi$, is essentially small and is closed under retracts.
repair: A retract is the colimit of an idempotent omega-chain; compactness is preserved by the indicated small colimits since pi^+-filtered colimits of sets commute with limits of size at most pi.

statement: The full image of $\operatorname{Ind}_\pi B\to\mathcal M$ equals the filtered-colimit envelope of $A$: bounded filtered-colimit closure plus $\pi^+$-filtered closure gives all filtered colimits.
notes: Unlike an arbitrary essential image, this Ind image is fully faithfully embedded because the objects of B are compact in M.

statement: Definition 4.13.35. An L-accessible object class is a replete accessible, accessibly embedded full subcategory of an accessible category with all filtered colimits, closed under those colimits.
Footnote 158: L-accessible object classes are closed under small intersections and finite unions.
repair: Use a common large rank for intersections, and the finite cofinal-union lemma for unions.

statement: Footnotes 158–159: inverse images of L-accessible classes under functors preserving all filtered colimits are L-accessible.
repair: Such a functor is accessible between accessible categories; combine 4.13.31 with preservation of filtered colimits.

statement: Proposition 4.13.36. Assume $\pi$ useful and $\mathcal S(\pi)$ closed under filtered colimits of size at most $\pi$. Then $\mathcal S$ is $\pi$-accessible iff membership of $x$ is equivalent to finality of $\mathcal S(\pi)/x\to\mathcal M_\pi/x$.
The same condition is equivalent to cofinal occurrence of $\mathcal S(\pi)$ in every L-$\pi$-adapted presentation, and remains equivalent when restricted to ordered index categories.
repair: The ordered implication uses Lemma 4.13.37, which supplies such a presentation without the earlier exponentiation restriction.

statement: One may test membership using one chosen L-$\pi$-adapted presentation of each object.
gap_or_error: The printed c-double-prime drops L from L-pi-adapted. Without the continuity condition arbitrary compact presentations do not have the cofinal-membership property.
repair: Read L-pi-adapted, as in c), c-prime and the immediately following lemma. For a counterexample without continuity, take two-element sets with constant nonidentity transition maps over pi-plus; their colimit is a singleton while no stage is a singleton.
notes: The statement is audited in its intended context; the weaker literal wording is not adopted.

statement: Lemma 4.13.37. Every object of an accessible category with all filtered colimits has an L-$\pi$-adapted presentation indexed by a small $\pi^+$-filtered poset, for each useful $\pi$.
repair: The filtered-subcategory construction supplies all four required properties; details are expanded in the p361 block.

statement: The index poset consists of filtered subcategories $J'\subset J$, each with at most $\pi$ arrows, where $J$ is a small skeleton of $\mathcal M_\pi/x$; set $x_{J'}=\varinjlim_{j\in J'}x_j$.
notes: These are subcategories, not full subcategories; full closure could destroy the cardinal bound.

statement: This poset is small, closed under filtered unions of at most $\pi$ members, and $J'\mapsto x_{J'}$ preserves those colimits; each $x_{J'}$ is $\pi^+$-presentable.
repair: Filtered union preserves finite cocone/equalization witnesses. Iterated colimits commute, and a colimit with at most pi arrows of pi-plus-presentables is pi-plus-presentable.

statement: The poset of bounded filtered subcategories is $\pi^+$-filtered: a family of at most $\pi$ members generates a subcategory with at most $\pi$ arrows, which admits a bounded filtered enlargement.
Lemma 4.13.38, first assertion. Any subcategory with at most $\pi$ arrows of a $\pi^+$-filtered category lies in a filtered subcategory with at most $\pi$ arrows.
repair: A simpler complete countable finite-witness closure proof is supplied; ordinary filteredness of the ambient category already suffices for this first assertion.

statement: If a cocone over $K$ can be chosen with vertex $e\notin K$, then $K$ admits a full inclusion into a subcategory $K'\subset J$ obtained by adding only $e$ and its chosen compatible incoming arrows; $e$ is terminal in $K'$.
notes: Fullness here is K in K-prime, not K-prime in J. This distinction is essential.

statement: The extra-vertex construction is available unless $J$ has a maximal object and $K$ contains all maximal objects, as in the exception stated in 4.13.38.

statement: A cocone over the at-most-$\pi$-arrow category $K$ is obtained by choosing a common target for its objects and simultaneously equalizing the at-most-$\pi$ compatibility pairs.

statement: Adjoining $p$ gives a subcategory whose new morphisms have normal form $v p^r u$, with $u,v$ in $K$ and $r\geq1$; composition stays in normal form because $p(v_1u_2)=p$.

statement: This one-endomorphism enlargement is filtered iff the sequence of powers of $p$ eventually stabilizes; a single equalizer need not achieve that.
gap_or_error: The printed explanation contains pv=pu, an ill-typed equation, and says u,v lie in K-prime where normal forms require K.

statement: Repeating the equalization construction countably often and taking the union produces a filtered subcategory containing $K$ with at most $\pi$ arrows.
gap_or_error: The printed equality Ob K_i=Ob J should read Ob K_i=Ob K in this exceptional-case construction.

statement: Corollary 4.13.39 defines the subsemigroup $\Sigma\subset\operatorname{End}_J(e)$ of endomorphisms equalizing all parallel $K$-arrows with target $e$; $\Sigma$ is nonempty and closed under multiplication.
notes: Nonemptiness uses pi-plus-filteredness and maximality of e in J, allowing a simultaneous equalizer to be returned to e.

statement: There is a countably generated nonempty subsemigroup $\Sigma_\infty\subset\Sigma$ whose associated one-object category is filtered.

statement: After making $e$ weakly terminal in $K$, the union of $\operatorname{Fl}K$ and arrows $vpu$ with $u,v\in\operatorname{Fl}K$ and $p\in\Sigma_\infty$ is the arrow set of a filtered category $K'$ on $\operatorname{Ob}K$.

statement: The normal form multiplication is $v'p'u'vpu=v'(p'p)u$, and arbitrary pairs of arrows into $e$ are equalized by some $qp_0\in\Sigma_\infty$.

statement: Theorem 4.14.1 defines the full category of functors from an essentially small category C to an accessible N sending a specified small family of cocones and cones to colimit cocones and limit cones, assuming N admits all those shapes.

statement: Footnote 163 conjectures that the target completeness assumptions in Theorem 4.14.1 can be dropped; it points forward to 4.14.16 for removal of the limit-shape assumption.

statement: Choosing a sufficiently large common useful pi identifies pi-accessible functors M→N with functors from a small skeleton C=M_pi to N; pi0-accessibility is then expressed by preserving bounded pi0-filtered colimits in C.

notes: The source notation Phi=Phi_pi [?] is an acknowledged local choice error; use the class of all small colimit shapes, reduced to a small bounded sketch.

statement: For adjunctions $L\dashv R$ and $L^\prime\dashv R^\prime$, the mate correspondence identifies natural transformations $R\to R^\prime$ with $L^\prime\to L$.

repair: Apply the dual of the representability theorem and its adjoint corollary, SGA4 I.8.12.7–8.12.8.
notes: No accessibility of the source or target is required beyond the stated pseudo-topos hypotheses.

statement: Corollary 4.14.11, covariant half: every small-limit-preserving $F:\mathcal M\to\mathbf{Set}$ on a locally presentable category is representable.

repair: Add accessibility of F, or the solution-set condition.
notes: The printed reference 8.3.12 should point to 8.13.2; that proposition explicitly assumes accessibility.

repair: Apply the dual special adjoint functor theorem, or the representability theorem with a small generating family.

statement: Footnote 166 identifies the Ind-categories of small categories, up to equivalence, with finitely accessible categories.

statement: Question 4.14.15: for every accessible $\mathcal N$, is the full category of epimorphisms accessible in $\mathcal N^{[1]}$?

statement: Epimorphisms are closed under retracts in the arrow category.

statement: Corollary 4.14.15.1: if accessible $\mathcal N$ has pushouts, its full category of epimorphisms is accessible and accessibly embedded in $\mathcal N^{[1]}$.
The functor $\gamma(x\to y)=(y\amalg_x y\to y)$ preserves all available colimits, hence is accessible.

repair: The self-pushout represents pairs of maps agreeing on x; its codiagonal is invertible precisely when every such pair is equal.

statement: Conjecture 4.14.16: one may remove the target existence assumptions in 4.14.1 and still obtain accessibility of the subcategory of diagrams that satisfy the prescribed universal cone conditions.

statement: 4.14.22 (proof). Replacing an essentially small base C by an equivalent small full subcategory does not change the section category up to equivalence.
notes: Used to make the products and sets of equations small; fibration hypotheses permit the transport.

statement: For a small base C and accessible fibres E_s, the products Π=∏_s E_s and Π′=∏_{λ:s→t} E_s are accessible.
repair: Choose a common sufficiently large regular accessibility cardinal exceeding the sizes of the indexing sets; products of the corresponding small generating subcategories generate.

statement: For a cleavage of a fibration p, F_λ=pr_s and G_λ=λ^*pr_t determine accessible functors F,G:Π⇉Π′.
gap_or_error: The printed s_1 in G_λ is already corrected editorially to t_0.
repair: Use G_λ=λ^*pr_t; choose one common rank for the small family of transition functors.

statement: A section f determines natural arrows α_λ(f):f(s)→λ^*f(t), hence a natural transformation α:Fε⇒Gε.
notes: Cartesian factorisation gives the arrows and naturality; no split cleavage is required.

statement: M′ is the inserter Ins(F,G): its objects are (X,u:FX→GX), and a morphism h satisfies G(h)u=vF(h).
The functor Γ(E/C)→M′ identifies the section category with a replete full subcategory of graph sections.
notes: A graph-section morphism is a family of vertical arrows commuting with all assigned arrows; this is exactly a natural transformation when the objects are functors.

statement: The full subcategory Γ(E/C)⊂M′ is cut out by the equations f(id_s)=id and f(μλ)=f(μ)f(λ).
notes: For a non-split cleavage the latter equation includes the canonical comparison λ*μ*≅(μλ)* when expressed in fibre coordinates.

statement: Each unit or composition equation is an equality between two natural transformations with values in a fibre, and the corresponding functor to the category of parallel arrows is accessible.
repair: Compute filtered colimits of graph sections pointwise at a common rank. The chosen pullback functors preserve those colimits, so the two comparison arrows do also.

statement: The full subcategory of equal parallel pairs (u,u) in E_s^{(0⇉1)} is accessible and accessibly embedded.
repair: It is equivalent to E_s^[1]; the diagonal inclusion preserves the relevant pointwise filtered colimits.

statement: The intersection of the inverse images of these equation subcategories is accessible and accessibly embedded in M′.
notes: Only a set of equations is imposed. The preceding inverse-image and intersection results apply.

statement: Lemma 4.14.22.1: the inserter of two accessible functors F,G:Π⇉Π′ between accessible categories is accessible; its projection to Π is accessible.
references: Positselski2024Limits, Theorem 4.1 (a more quantitative formulation with chain hypotheses); MakkaiPare1989, §5.1

statement: Ins(F,G) is equivalent to the full subcategory of pairs of arrows FX→Y←GX for which GX→Y is invertible.
repair: The quasi-inverse sends (X,Y,u,v) to (X,v^{-1}u); the reverse functor uses Y=GX and v=id. Invertibility is an accessible condition.

statement: The general fibration section theorem reduces to the opfibration section theorem for the parallel-arrow category, and the opfibration case admits the same reduction.
notes: This is a reduction of proof, not a claim that the remaining special case is elementary.

statement: 4.14.23. H: for every base arrow λ:[1]→C, the pullback E_λ=E×_C[1] is accessible and its projection p_λ:E_λ→[1] is accessible.
H implies that every strict fibre E_s is accessible and that the endpoint inclusions E_s→E_λ are accessible.
repair: Each endpoint is the inverse image of a replete accessible singleton subcategory of [1].

statement: Lemma 4.14.23.1: for a fibration or opfibration over [1], H is equivalent to accessibility of both fibres and of the corresponding transition functor.
gap_or_error: The displayed adjunction orientations in the necessity proof are reversed.
repair: For the opfibration φ, the extension barφ:E→E_1 is left adjoint to E_1→E. For the fibration ψ, the extension tildeψ:E→E_0 is right adjoint to E_0→E. Either orientation still invokes the valid adjacent lemma. Sufficiency follows from 4.14.24.

statement: As printed, the inclusion E_1→E in the opfibration has a right adjoint, and the inclusion E_0→E in the fibration has a left adjoint.
gap_or_error: Both adjunction directions are reversed, and the target of the displayed composite for ψ is also E_1 instead of E_0.
repair: Replace by barφ ⊣ inclusion E_1→E, and inclusion E_0→E ⊣ tildeψ. These follow immediately from the cross-Hom descriptions on page 413.
notes: Confirmed in authoritative PDF leaf 37; preserved as an edition/source slip.

statement: Lemma 4.14.23.2: each member of an adjunction F:E⇄E′:G between accessible categories is accessible.
repair: Choose a small strong generating set of presentable objects ξ of E and a common regular κ at which ξ and Fξ are presentable and both categories have κ-filtered colimits. The adjunction identifies Hom(ξ,G−) with Hom(Fξ,−), and conservativity detects the comparison for G.

statement: Footnote 172 proposes weakening accessibility of E to existence of a small generating subcategory, while retaining that all objects of E′ are accessible.
gap_or_error: The displayed proof uses preservation of filtered colimits by the representables Hom_E(ξ,−), in addition to conservativity. This is automatic in the lemma, but is not explained under the footnote’s weaker assumptions.
repair: For the proof supplied here, require a small strong generator consisting of presentable objects and the relevant filtered colimits in E. No assertion of a counterexample to every interpretation of the footnote is made.
notes: The main lemma is unaffected; the literal weakening is not certified by this audit.

statement: The collage of H:E_0^op×E_1→Set has the given categories as full subcategories, cross-Homs H(x_0,x_1), and no arrows from E_1 to E_0.
notes: Grothendieck calls E_0 open and E_1 closed; these mean a sieve and its complementary cosieve.

statement: For an opfibration classified by φ:E_0→E_1 the cross-Hom is Hom_{E_1}(φx_0,x_1); for a fibration classified by ψ:E_1→E_0 it is Hom_{E_0}(x_0,ψx_1).

Proposition 4.14.24: for a collage E, (a) E and E→[1] are accessible; (b) E is accessible and both fibre inclusions are accessible; (c) E_0,E_1 are accessible, every H(x_0,−) is accessible, and one common rank makes every H(−,x_1) send filtered colimits to limits; these conditions are equivalent.
notes: Accessibility of a contravariant Set-valued functor means the stated colimit-to-limit preservation; it does not assert accessibility of Set^op.

statement: Accessible transition functors φ or ψ give the two cross-Hom preservation conditions of 4.14.24(c).
repair: For φ use its common colimit-preservation rank and presentability of φx_0; for ψ compose H(x_0,−)=Hom(x_0,ψ−), and use representability in the first variable.

statement: (a)⇒(b) follows by inverse images of endpoints; (b)⇒(c) follows from accessibility of the inclusions and of representables.
repair: For the uniform contravariant condition use one colimit-preservation rank of E_0→E; representable Hom_E(−,x_1) then converts these colimits to limits for every x_1 at once.

statement: One can choose π_0 useful for E_0 and a larger π with π^{π_0}=π, useful for E_1, bounding the small generating subcategory and all functors H(a,−) for π_0-presentable a.
notes: The smallness of the chosen skeleton is essential to obtaining one bound.

statement: E(π) is the full subcategory whose objects are the union of the π-presentable objects of E_0 and E_1.
Under the chosen bounds the collage E admits the specified filtered colimits; both fibre inclusions and E→[1] preserve them.
gap_or_error: The first sentence of the proof prints E where E_1 is intended; the later reference to case a for a tail in E_1 is inaccurate.
repair: A diagram staying in E_0 has a universal colimit in E by the H(−,x_1) condition. Once a filtered diagram enters the cosieve E_1 its tail stays there and has its colimit in E_1. The closed-fibre argument applies to nonempty diagrams, as all filtered diagrams are.

statement: Under these colimit-preservation hypotheses, a π-presentable object of E is π-presentable in its own fibre, so E_π⊂E(π).
repair: Restrict the representing functor to filtered diagrams in its fibre; the inclusion is fully faithful and preserves their colimits.

statement: At the chosen larger cardinal π, a π-presentable object in either fibre is π-presentable in E, so E(π)=E_π.
repair: For x_0 in E_0 express x_0 as a π-small π_0-filtered colimit of π_0-presentables. Then H(x_0,−) is a π-small limit of the functors H(a,−), which preserves π-large filtered colimits. For x_1 in E_1, cross-Homs to E_0 are empty and the other case is internal.
notes: The calculation is the content of the cited SGA 4 I 9.6(ii); presentability ranks are enlarged, not fixed arbitrarily.

statement: The canonical Ind_π(E(π))→E is essentially surjective, hence an equivalence, because each fibre is generated by its π-presentable objects and its inclusion preserves the generating colimits.

Corollary 4.14.25(1), literally: E and E_0 have π-large filtered colimits and E_0→E preserves them iff E_0 has them and all H(−,x_1) preserve them contravariantly; it then asserts existence of the same colimits in E_1.
gap_or_error: The right-hand side lacks the hypothesis that E_1 has the specified filtered colimits.
repair: Add that E_1 satisfies L_π. The preceding proof then establishes the equivalence. Counterexample: E_0=1, E_1 the ordinal κ=π^+ with its order category, H constant singleton. The printed right side holds, but the κ-directed identity diagram in E_1 has no upper bound or colimit in the collage.
notes: Confirmed PDF leaf 41. This is a source statement defect, not a transcription mistake. The hypotheses used in Proposition 4.14.24 already include the missing colimits at the chosen rank.

statement: Corollary 4.14.25(2): the cardinal bounds and preservation hypotheses from the proof identify E_π with E(π).
gap_or_error: The quantified x_0 is printed as belonging to E_{π_0}, where E_{0,π_0} is intended.
repair: Read the quantified objects as the π_0-presentables of the open fibre; retain the common-rank colimit conditions of the preceding proof and corrected part (1).

statement: Corollary 4.14.25(3): if π also is useful for E_1, then π is useful for E and E≃Ind_π(E(π)).
notes: The power bound makes π useful for E_0; the additional assumption supplies generation and colimits in E_1.

statement: H is equivalent to H′: every fibre is accessible, every cross-Hom H_λ(x,−) is accessible, and for each λ one rank uniformly makes all H_λ(−,y) send filtered colimits to limits.
repair: Apply the collage criterion 4.14.24 to each E_λ.

statement: Theorem 4.14.26: under H and smallness of C, Γ(E/C) is accessible and all evaluation functors Γ(E/C)→E_s are accessible.
gap_or_error: The proof calls the equation argument sorital; it omits the explicit accessibility check for composition constraints in the absence of a cleavage.
repair: Use the accessible inserter built from the endpoint inclusions E_s→E_λ. The comparison functors to the relevant arrow categories preserve sufficiently filtered colimits: endpoint inclusions create the needed cocones and composition is determined by them. A small joint equifier imposes identities and composition. Details supplied in the p423 block.

statement: Theorem 4.14.26 admits refinements analogous to 4.14.18, including pointwise filtered colimits and eventual pointwise presentability bounds.
repair: Choose one regular cardinal controlling all fibre categories, endpoint inclusions, and the small family of equations. Pointwise presentability then follows by the hom-set equalizer formula; an eventual converse requires the usual enlarged bound.
notes: The source explicitly leaves the precise formulation to the reader.

statement: For arbitrary p satisfying H, define Π=∏_sE_s and Π′=∏_λE_λ, with F_λ=i_λpr_s and G_λ=j_λpr_t; these categories and functors are accessible.
The corresponding inserter is the category of graph sections, and its full subcategory satisfying the unit and composition equations is the actual section category.
repair: An arrow in E_λ from its 0-fibre to its 1-fibre is exactly an arrow of E over λ. Natural transformations in the inserter are precisely vertical graph transformations.

statement: The evaluation functors are the composites Γ(E/C)→M′→Π→E_s and hence accessible.
gap_or_error: The projection M′→Π is printed as a hooked inclusion, but it forgets arrow data and is not a full-subcategory inclusion.
repair: Read the middle arrow as an ordinary accessible forgetful functor.

statement: H1: all fibres E_s are accessible.
H2: for each λ:s→t there is a common rank π_λ such that E_s has π_λ-large filtered colimits and H_λ(−,y) takes them to limits for every y∈E_t.
H3: for every λ:s→t and x∈E_s, H_λ(x,−):E_t→Set is accessible.
Proposition 4.15.1, first conclusion: H1 and H2 imply accessibility of every fibre inclusion i_s:E_s→E.
repair: Split Hom_E(x,y) as the disjoint union of Hom_λ(x,y) over λ:s→t. Since a filtered indexing category is nonempty and connected, taking the limit preserves this decomposition by the constant base arrow. H2 supplies each bijection.
notes: H3 is not used.

statement: The base C is sans projecteurs if every idempotent endomorphism of every object of C is the identity.
notes: This is stronger than idempotent completeness.

statement: Proposition 4.15.1, second conclusion: if C is small and sans projecteurs and H1–H3 hold, then E is accessible and p:E→C is accessible.
gap_or_error: The proof uses the deferred constant-cofinal-subdiagram lemma; the explicit corollary also omits π_0≥sup_λ π_λ, required for its presentation calculation.
repair: Choose the base bound strictly greater than |C|, as proved later in 4.15.10–11 (ms462–463), and choose π_0 already useful for all fibres and at least every π_λ. Then the small-presentation argument proves the qualitative proposition. A complete finite-poset test and counterexample to the printed rank bounds are supplied in the p425 development.
notes: The official complete chapter was checked at ms430–432 and452,462–463; these continuations are outside the attached leaves.

statement: Corollary 4.15.2(a): if π_1 bounds the π_λ for all arrows with source s, then i_s preserves π_1-large filtered colimits.
gap_or_error: The source first says source t instead of source s, then uses π_0 in the proof although the bound is π_1.
repair: Use source s and π_1 throughout the proof on pages 427–428.

statement: Corollary 4.15.2(b): if C is sans projecteurs and π_1 bounds |C| and all π_λ, then E has π_1-large filtered colimits and p preserves them.
gap_or_error: The last clause prints π rather than π_1. The deferred lemma is ultimately proved in the chapter only with π_1>|C|, not the boundary equality.
repair: Read π_1-accessible and strengthen the base bound to π_1>|C|. The source itself supplies this repair in 4.15.10–11 (ms462–463).

statement: Corollary 4.15.2(c) chooses π_0 useful for each fibre and π_1 bounding π_0, |C|, the transition ranks, the sizes of the small fibre generators, and the accessibility ranks of H_λ(x,−) for π_0-presentable x.
notes: Only a small family of such data is involved, so a common bound exists.

statement: Under these bounds, if π^{π_0}=π≥π_1, each π-presentable object of a fibre is π-presentable in E.
gap_or_error: The printed hypotheses do not require π_0≥π_λ. A π_0-filtered presentation cannot be passed through a functor known only to preserve π_λ-large colimits when π_λ>π_0.
repair: Require π_0≥sup_λ π_λ in addition to usefulness for the fibres. Counterexample in ZFC: over [1], take both fibres Set and transition φ(X)=X^K with |K|=aleph1. Let π_0=aleph0, π_1=2^{aleph1}, π=beth_{omega1}. Then π^{aleph0}=π and all the printed bounds hold, but |X|=π in the lower fibre gives |φX|=π^{aleph1}>π, so X is not π-presentable in the collage. Full proof in the p425 block.
notes: The official continuation at ms430 explicitly uses π_0-accessibility of the contravariant H_λ, revealing the omitted condition. The qualitative proposition is repaired by enlarging π_0.

statement: As printed in 4.15.2(c), the subcategory E_π itself satisfies L_{π_1}, hence L_π.
gap_or_error: The text needs colimit existence in E, not in its subcategory of π-presentable objects; a presentable-object subcategory is not generally closed under arbitrarily large filtered colimits.
repair: Replace E_π by E in this sentence. Even in Set, a sufficiently long increasing diagram of sets of size at most π can have a larger union.
notes: Confirmed PDF leaf 44; retained in the transcription.

statement: As printed in 4.15.2(c), Ind_π(E_{s,π})→E is an equivalence for a single fixed fibre s.
gap_or_error: A single fibre cannot generate the other fibres; for example the identity functor [1]→[1] has terminal fibres but nonterminal total category.
repair: Replace E_{s,π} by E(π), the union of the small objects of all fibres. The canonical functor is then fully faithful by their ambient presentability and essentially surjective by fibrewise generation.
notes: Confirmed PDF leaf 44.

statement: Corollary 4.15.2(d): under the same hypotheses E(π)=E_π, not just E(π)⊂E_π.
gap_or_error: With exactly the printed bounds, the equality fails because the inclusion asserted in part c can fail; see the power-functor counterexample.
repair: After adding π_0≥sup_λ π_λ and using a strict bound over |C|, the reverse inclusion is proved in the official continuation at ms431–432: presentables are retracts of fibrewise small objects; the image of a retraction idempotent in a projector-free base is the identity, so the retract is vertical and small in its fibre.
notes: The forward inclusion needs the separate rank repair; the strict fibre need not be full when the base has nonidentity endomorphisms.

statement: For a filtered diagram in E_s, the comparison Hom_E(colim x_i,y)→lim Hom_E(x_i,y) is a map in Set/Hom_C(s,t), and is bijective exactly when each λ-component is bijective.
notes: Nonemptiness and connectedness of the indexing category ensure the base-arrow label is constant in a compatible family.

statement: Lemma 4.15.3: if |C|≤π and C has no nonidentity idempotents, every π-large filtered diagram in C has a cofinal subsystem whose objects are one fixed object and whose transition arrows are identities.
gap_or_error: The proof is deferred to ms452 and still conditional there on 4.8.13. The verified later Corollary4.15.10 establishes the needed result with π>|C|.
repair: For all qualitative accessibility applications enlarge π so that π>|C|. The exact equality-bound formulation is not certified by this audit; no assertion that it is an open modern problem is made.
notes: Official complete Chapter XVIII consulted at ms452 and462–463, outside the supplied extract.

statement: For a rigid base, meaning End_C(s)={id_s} for all s, the constant-cofinal-subdiagram lemma is immediate.
repair: For a directed poset indexing category, a colouring by the ≤π object labels has a cofinal colour: otherwise choose one excluded tail for each colour and take a common upper bound. All arrows between that colour are identities by rigidity. A cofinal directed-poset replacement gives the categorical form.

statement: Assuming Lemma 4.15.3, existence of colimits in E and their preservation by p reduce to a constant-base diagram in a single fibre.
notes: The argument is valid; the verified strict-bound version of the deferred lemma suffices for qualitative accessibility.

statement: For the presentability comparison, the same reduction makes the target system lie in E_t and decomposes the comparison by arrows λ:s→t.
gap_or_error: The attached extract ends mid-sentence. The continuation at ms430–431 additionally invokes an unassumed π_0-rank preservation property.
repair: Complete the calculation after requiring π_0≥sup_λ π_λ and using the strict base bound. Without this repair the exact cardinal assertion is false, as the p425 counterexample proves.
